UseCaseDescription: Prabhix Technologies runs a multi-tenant B2B SaaS platform (OneOps for operations, Mailroom for shared-mailbox helpdesk, MobiStack for mobile-repair shops). All mail is transactional and originates from an action the recipient took inside one of our products: account verification and password reset, login and security alerts, invoices and payment receipts, order and job-status notifications, and agent replies to support tickets that the customer themselves opened by writing to a shared mailbox. We do not send newsletters, promotions or purchased lists, and we have no bulk-send workflow. Recipients are our paying tenants, their named staff users, and the end customers of those tenants who have contacted them. Consent: every address enters the system either as a self-registered account (double opt-in via a verification mail) or as the sender of an inbound support message, so the first outbound mail to any address is always a reply or a confirmation the person is expecting. Unsubscribe: transactional notification categories are individually switchable per user in account settings, and every non-critical mail carries a one-click preference link; verification, security and billing mail is not unsubscribable by design and is documented as such at sign-up. Bounces and complaints: the SES event stream is delivered over SNS to a verified webhook that our backend authenticates (signature verified against the Amazon SNS signing certificate) and processes automatically. Hard bounces and complaints suppress the address in our own database immediately, mark the recipient undeliverable, stop all further sends to it, and raise it in the operator console for review; soft bounces are retried with exponential backoff and then suppressed. We track bounce and complaint rates per sending domain and alert on them. All sending is queued through a transactional outbox with per-tenant rate limits, so a runaway loop cannot produce a send spike. Sending domain prabhixtechnologies.com is verified with DKIM (three CNAMEs published), SPF and DMARC. Expected volume at launch is roughly 500-2,000 messages per day, growing with tenant count.
